The classification for neural network model for their paper, is based on cosine similarity of vectors from labeled example instances and unlabeled text data for the senses. Using the WordNet and the New Oxford American Dictionary as sense inventory, there was significant performance results. They claim that the LSTM language model produced the best results [7]. Long-short term memory is a type of recurrent neural network model. The paper discussed the use of semi-supervised methods since obtaining large data is not easy. Vector representation of words and context was built using a neural network based language model (NNLM) and two NNLM were discussed [7]. The CBOW computes a context vector from word contexts and then predicts a target sense while the LSTM is trained to predict held out words from a sentence [7]. Kågebäck and Salomonsson present a bidirectional long short-term memory network model to disambiguate word sense in their paper [2]. The bidirectional version of the LSTM takes into account two LSTMs in each state, one for words before and one for word after. The model consists of a softmax layer, hidden layer and a bi-directional LSTM. The bidirectional LSTM and hidden layer for all sense and type, share the parameters, while the softmax is parameterized by word type which decides the bias vector and weight matrix for each word type [2]. 15 The proposed BLSTM model by Kågebäck and Salomonsson performed better than previous state- of-the-art score for the Senseval-2 dataset [2]. Work has also been done for word sense disambiguation using neural networks with refined concept co-occurrence information, which is automated and does not require hand coding large data, as presented by Chung, Kang, Moon, and Lee in their paper [8]. As described before, many word sense disambiguation is done using neural network with varying precision and efficiency. They are powerful models to use and their effectiveness on Bangla language processing will provide further insight of their practical usefulness on different languages. 2.3 Supervised Machine Learning Lexical sample word sense disambiguation task is commonly done using supervised learning algorithms to detect the correct sense. Firstly, the classifier has to be built using the training dataset. Important and relevant features from the dataset needs to be extracted. Which features are chosen and how they are refined tend to differ based on different models and systems. Therefore, some pre-processing of the raw text data instances has to be done. A feature vector is built encoded as numerical values for corresponding lexical data. Collocational and Bag-of-words features are two types of feature classes. Collocational features hold information of the specific positions to the left and right of the target word [4]. The collocational feature vector used for supervised word sense disambiguation, as described in [4], with a two word window to the left and to the right of the target word follows the following structure: [𝑤𝑜𝑟𝑑𝑖−2, 𝑃𝑂𝑆𝑖−2, 𝑤𝑜𝑟𝑑𝑖−1, 𝑃𝑂𝑆𝑖−1, 𝑤𝑜𝑟𝑑𝑖+1, 𝑃𝑂𝑆𝑖+1, 𝑤𝑜𝑟𝑑𝑖+2, 𝑃𝑂𝑆𝑖+2]. 16 This feature v
executive_digest.findings_and_conclusions: and Future Work 5.1 Conclusion This thesis presented and discussed the effectiveness of word sense disambiguation using supervised learning and a deep neural network classifier on both English and Bangla data. After collecting the SENSEVAL 2 lexical sample data set and applying the individual models, it was evident that the K near neighbors supervised classifier performed with satisfactory results. The accuracy score turned out to be much better than anticipated. On the other hand, the Neural network classifier still has room for improvement. The neural network classifier had significant noise and major variance in accuracy. The neural network implementation requires even further experiments and tweaking in terms of layers, pre-processing and neuron unit count. In both models, the English dataset resulted in more standard and accurate results, since the dataset used, SENSEVAL 2, was a large and standard one. However, the Bangla dataset results are yet to be more accurate, since the data were hand labelled and was relatively small. A larger dataset of Bangla sense tagged data would work even better and would result in a better accuracy score. In general, both the systems were able to perform fairly efficiently and effectively with very fast response time. The systems and implementations presented in this thesis definitely hold practical value in natural language processing and with more experiments, better results can be achieved in the future. 34 5.2 Future Works: There were limitations in analyzing the word sense disambiguation models on Bangla language due to the lack of sense tagged resources. In the future, I would like to further investigate and improve the systems on Bangla using a larger dataset and perhaps newer models. Additionally, I would like to improve the deep learning system and implement it with speech to build a stable and efficient intelligent system that can have a fluid and clear conversation with a human in multiple languages. 35

evaluation.detailed_reasoning: This candidate triad (Rank 24, mean edge cosine = 0.985026) represents a textbook topological artifact arising from high-dimensional embedding biases rather than genuine scientific synergy. The near-unity pairwise cosine similarities (P1-P2: 0.9832, P2-P3: 0.9869, P1-P3: 0.9850) are entirely driven by institutional repository boilerplate, structural metadata, and identical dissertation formatting templates. Paper 1 (Ciutad Castejón) is an oncological biophysics thesis investigating photodynamic therapy (PDT) utilizing the photosensitizer BBr2HPC combined with hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) to overcome hypoxia-mediated resistance in WiDr colorectal carcinoma cells. Paper 2 (Monrós Coma, advised by Z. Niu) is an electrical engineering master's report from UPC/Tsinghua University focusing on green cellular telecommunications, modeling 3-sector base-station cell zooming coverage (CZC) and multi-hop relay stations (MRC) to cut RF power consumption by up to 53% under varying SINR and traffic loads. Paper 3 is an NLP thesis evaluating lexical sample word sense disambiguation (WSD) for Bangla and English across SENSEVAL-2 corpora using K-nearest neighbors (KNN) and Bidirectional LSTMs over collocational n-gram feature windows. The embedding graph collapsed these three disparate works into a tight 2-simplex because all three files are university master's theses containing verbatim academic structural boilerplate (e.g., 'CONTENTS', 'List of Figures', 'The aim of this chapter is to expose all the theoretical foundations', 'Advisor: Professor...', 'Future Works', and section numbering tokens). Thematically, their core domains—in vitro photomedicine, cellular telecommunications, and computational lexical semantics—share zero direct ontology. However, from a high-order cybernetic and methodological perspective, an interdisciplinary researcher can abstract three complementary functional primitives: (1) localized resource depletion in heterogeneous media (hypoxia during PDT/singlet oxygen consumption), (2) spatial multi-hop routing and dynamic resource/power 'zooming' under constraints, and (3) context-dependent sequence classification under noise. Thus, while the triad co-occurrence is spurious, non-trivial trans-disciplinary bridges can be synthetically constructed.

research_statements.title: Distributed Optoelectronic Micro-Relay Networks with Dynamic Sector Zooming for Hypoxia-Mitigated Colorectal Photodynamic Therapy
research_statements.research_statement: Deploying an intraluminal array of bio-compatible optoelectronic micro-relay nodes operating under an adaptive sector-zooming power protocol will overcome deep-tissue optical attenuation and transient hypoxia during colon cancer photodynamic therapy; by executing on-chip deep neural sequence classification of local optical coherence and oxygenation profiles, the network dynamically throttles photon fluence to match localized hyperbaric oxygen re-perfusion, thereby increasing WiDr colorectal cancer apoptotic cytotoxicity by >40% while reducing non-target mucosal thermal injury.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Integrates Paper 1's combination of BBr2HPC photosensitization and hyperbaric oxygen replenishment with Paper 2's multi-hop relay station (MRC) and 3-sector cell zooming coverage (CZC) power-management framework, using Paper 3's context-windowed deep neural classification to resolve local tissue metabolic states from real-time optoelectronic sensor streams.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Demonstrates the first closed-loop, distributed bio-photonic relay network that dynamically synchronizes optical fluence vectors with localized oxygen replenishment waves in solid tumors.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Resolves the self-quenching rate bottleneck of photodynamic therapy, wherein continuous illumination exhausts local molecular oxygen faster than diffusion allows, inducing acute treatment resistance.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Ingestible or flexible endoscopic smart stents for non-surgical debulking of obstructive, inoperable colorectal adenocarcinomas.

research_statements.title: Deep Contextual Sequence Disambiguation of Polysemic Bio-Impedance Signatures for Targeted Hyperbaric Photodynamic Actuation
research_statements.research_statement: A deep neural classification framework incorporating collocational feature extraction and bidirectional recurrent layers will resolve semantic ambiguity ('polysemy') in multi-frequency bio-impedance and fluorescence lifetime backscatter tokens, discriminating between viable hypoxic adenocarcinoma, necrotic tissue debris, and normal intestinal mucosa with >95% specificity to gate localized hyperbaric oxygen and laser micro-actuation.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Directly maps Paper 3's lexical sample word sense disambiguation architecture (BLSTM, collocational n-gram windows) onto continuous physiological multi-sensor spectra, enabling Paper 1's combined PDT/HBOT regimen to be triggered selectively at tumor coordinates, while implementing Paper 2's power sleep-modes when sensors detect non-malignant tissue contexts.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Establishes a rigorous mathematical mapping between natural language word sense disambiguation algorithms and multi-spectral tissue phenotype identification in ambiguous tumor microenvironments.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Eliminates diagnostic ambiguity and false-positive therapeutic triggering caused by overlapping spectral characteristics of inflammatory mucosa, tumor hypoxia, and post-radiation necrosis.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Real-time AI diagnostic guidance software integrated into clinical colonoscopes and photodynamic surgical tools.

research_statements.title: Energy-Harvesting Implantable Relay Architecture for Continuous Telemetric Monitoring Inside Clinical Hyperbaric Chambers
research_statements.research_statement: Implementing a 3-sector multihop relay communication protocol with traffic-adaptive cell zooming across intra-abdominal and trans-dermal sensor nodes will maintain an error-free (>99.9% packet yield) telemetric data link from deep colorectal tumors through steel hyperbaric oxygen chambers, reducing implant transmitter power consumption by >50% through deep neural channel-state disambiguation under severe multi-path attenuation.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Applies Paper 2's wireless multihop relay station (RS) topologies and sector-based power-zooming to biomedical implants, utilizes Paper 3's supervised feature-vector classification to disambiguate corrupted RF/acoustic telemetry packets, and solves the physical communication barrier of operating within Paper 1's 1-bar hyperbaric oxygen steel environment.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: First energy-optimized wireless communication standard capable of high-fidelity, bidirectional physiological telemetry across sealed metal hyperbaric enclosures.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Overcomes the severe radiofrequency shielding and tissue attenuation losses that prevent continuous patient physiological monitoring during hyperbaric oncology sessions.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Implantable and wearable telemetry platforms for oncology patients undergoing hyperbaric oxygenation and systemic radiotherapy or chemotherapy.

research_statements.title: Spatial Context Disambiguation and Multi-Agent Power Zooming for In Silico Tumor Microenvironment Digital Twins
research_statements.research_statement: Formulating solid tumor spatial histopathology as an ordered contextual sequence permits Bidirectional LSTM classifiers to disambiguate ambiguous metabolic phenotypes (differentiating senescent G0/G1-arrested cells from terminal necrosis), enabling a multi-hop resource-allocation engine derived from cell-zooming heuristics to compute optimal multi-source laser fluence and hyperbaric oxygen schedules that lower the effective in vitro EC50 in simulated WiDr colon carcinoma cohorts.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Fuses Paper 3's contextual sequence disambiguation to interpret spatial transcriptomic/flow-cytometric data, Paper 2's sector cell-zooming algorithms to balance simulated optical/chemical resource delivery, and Paper 1's empirical MTT cell cycle and apoptotic/necrotic kinetic profiles.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Unifies computational linguistics, wireless cellular scheduling, and tumor biophysics into an algorithmic digital twin for personalized micro-dosimetry.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Replaces crude trial-and-error dosimetry in photodynamic oncology with an analytical, spatially resolved optimization pipeline.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Clinical treatment-planning software for interventional radiologists and oncologists designing personalized PDT and radiation beam protocols.

research_statements.title: Autonomous Bio-Robotic Relay Swarms with Edge Semantic Disambiguation for Colon Adenocarcinoma Eradication
research_statements.research_statement: An autonomous micro-robotic swarm utilizing ad-hoc multihop relay clustering and sleep-mode sector zooming will navigate the colorectal lumen, employing an embedded neural semantic classifier to disambiguate local biochemical cues (pH, ROS, pO2) and coordinate targeted micro-photonic activation with localized oxygen micro-bubble release, increasing WiDr colon cancer necrotic clearance by >60% while expanding swarm operational longevity by >45%.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Translates Paper 1's biochemical mechanism of singlet oxygen generation and hyperbaric oxygen sensitization into mobile microrobotics, uses Paper 2's base-station turning-off and multihop relay routing (MRC/CZC) to conserve swarm battery resources, and embeds Paper 3's lightweight neural disambiguation engine for real-time edge decision-making.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Pioneers the synthesis of swarm telecommunications, contextual edge intelligence, and targeted photochemical oncology in active autonomous biomaterials.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Solves the dual trade-offs of micro-robotic energy exhaustion and off-target chemical/photodynamic toxicity in deep gastrointestinal lumens.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Minimally invasive, ingestible autonomous micro-devices for early detection and single-session eradication of precancerous polyps and non-resectable colonic tumors.

paper_1.title: Photodynamic therapy improvement with hyperbaric oxygen therapy for human colon cancer treatment

executive_digest.abstract_and_aims: Nowadays, colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer worldwide. There are some therapies to treat this cancer, such as radiotherapy and chemotherapy. However, their efficacy can be decreased or completely inhibited by one characteristic of the tumor cells, hypoxia. Recently, has appeared one alternative therapy for those patients with inoperable colon cancer and it uses light sources to induce cell death by the production of singlet oxygen and other species of ROS. This therapy is called photodynamic therapy (PDT) but its effectiveness can be affected too by the hypoxic tumor cells. To increase the efficacy of PDT treatment it has been used the hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT), which overcomes the hypoxic state of cancer cells. The combined therapies have been applied using different conditions and their effect has been analyzed by MTT assay and cell cycle and cellular viability analysis by cytometry. The obtained results revealed that combination of PDT and HBOT is promising and that results of combination of PDT followed by HBOT during 60 minutes should be further studied. -11-

Metastasis is the main cause of dead by cancer. One of the cancers more diagnosed between men and women is colorectal cancer. (WHO; U.S National Library of Medicine) Colorectal cancer is formed in the tissues of the colon or in the tissues of the rectum, both in the large intestine. Most colorectal cancers are adenocarcinomas, cancers that begin in cells that make and release mucus and other fluids. executive_digest.findings_and_conclusions: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has been accepted as an alternative treatment for cancer, especially for solid tumors like carcinomas. It has some advantages over the current cancer chemotherapy and radiation therapy in terms of less adverse effects and targeted delivery. PDT requires three elements: light, a photosensitizer and molecular oxygen; (Shao et al. 2012) and is able to induce cell death by oxidative stress trough activation with light of a non-toxic photosensitizer. (Teixo 2013; Triesscheijn et al. 2006) The efficacy of PDT can be diminished because of regions of hypoxia, areas with a poorer oxygenation also present in colorectal cancer, suggested as an adverse prognostic factor for patient outcome. (Sudhakar et al. 2013; Vaupel and Mayer 2007) To alter the hypoxic state and improve treatment outcome it is used the hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT). (Daruwalla and Christophi 2006; Ogawa et al. 2013) Four possible treatments have been studied to improve PDT outcome in WiDr cell line: PDT+HBO 30min, PDT+HBO 60min, HBO 30min+PDT and HBO 60min+PDT. For PDT it has been used the photosensitizing agent BBr2HPC and irradiation with 10J, and for HBOT it has been applied, 1bar of 100% O2. To study their outcome, metabolic activity assay with MTT have been performed 24h and 48h after the treatment revealing an improvement from EC50=58,50nM of PDT treatment alone (Laranjo 2014) to EC50=17,96nM of PDT+HBOT 60min, both assays 24h after the therapy. The value of R2 does not reach 0,90 and more assays should be realized to have a better value for the fitting results and a Olga Ciutad Castejón -57- definitive decision about the best therapy, as the results for all the therapies analyzed 24h after the treatment are similar. To analyze the cytotoxicity effects of the treatment, two flow cytometry analysis have been performed: cellular viability assay and cell cycle analysis. To compare the effects of the different therapies, 24h after the treatment four conditions have been subjected to study: control, PDT, HBOT and PDT+HBOT 60min. As mentioned before, the combined therapy analyzed should had been the best of the eight studied before, PDT+HBOT 30min 24h after the treatment. To confirm the cellular effects of the colorectal cancer therapy, both assays of flow cytometry should be repeated studying the therapy with better EC50 and R 2. The cellular viability assay showed an increased percentage of necrotic cells, although that should be preferable apoptosis. In regard to cell cycle analysis, it has not shown differences but it can indicate not allow the cell duplication or in other words, the therapy does not allow colorectal cancer cell proliferate. paper_3.title: An analysis of word sense disambiguation in Bangla and English using supervised learning and a deep neural network classifier

executive_digest.abstract_and_aims: Word sense disambiguation is a significant task in natural language processing and addresses an old problem in the field of computational linguistics. Word sense disambiguation facilitates tasks like machine translation, information retrieval, text-to-speech and other application systems. Sense ambiguity is introduced because certain words for a given language can have multiple meanings. Word sense disambiguation involves identifying the correct sense of a word for a given context. Bangla language has a few cases of word sense ambiguity. Many machine learning algorithms have already been applied to disambiguate word sense including few implementations of neural networks. However, many existing word sense disambiguation systems using supervised learning and neural networks were focused only on English data. And an evaluation of their implementation on Bangla data is necessary. This thesis attempts to analyze and present results when using an updated deep neural network classifier and supervised learning algorithm for word sense disambiguation on a Bangla dataset and on an English dataset. A pre-processor for the dataset was constructed to appropriately extract features from the context sentences to build sets of refined feature vectors which are fed into the neural network. 9
executive_digest.introduction_and_motivation: 1.1 Overview Word Sense Disambiguation for most systems involves choosing or classifying the correct sense for a given word in a sentence. Existence of homonyms in languages introduces ambiguity for word senses. Since certain words can have multiple meanings depending on the context of the sentence, the syntactic structure of that given word does not provide sufficient clues to the word’s correct sense. Therefore, the context words that occur before and after the target word has to be taken into account for accurate sense classification. There are many existing word sense disambiguation algorithms and systems. Word sense disambiguation has many applications and is an important task that helps and facilitates other natural language processing tasks like machine translation, question-answering, information retrieval and text-to-speech systems. Machine learning techniques have been applied on tackling word sense disambiguation exercises before. Supervised learning algorithms have shown to be very effective at disambiguating word senses when it comes to the lexical sample task [1]. Most supervised machine learning algorithms for lexical sample tasks learn from the training corpora, by taking in the features and labels to build an appropriate classifier. This classifier can then be evaluated by using a test data set. The classifier is able to label the senses after fed with test features. The tagged senses are then evaluated for accuracy. Deep learning and artificial neural networks have shown to be effective at dealing with complex problems and tasks. Neural(s). Therefore, deep neural 10 network classifier for disambiguating word sense is an approach that is justifiable. There are existing models of word sense disambiguation based on neural networks. An analysis of the sense tagging task with an updated neural network on Bangla language as well English data will provide further insights into how effective they are on natural language processing. 1.2  Objective and Goals Neural networks have many applications and have been applied to word sense disambiguation. However, there is scope for further application and a revision of newer neural network models. This thesis attempts to dive deeper into the performance and efficiency of deep neural networks when used for disambiguating word senses on a standard SENSEVAL-2 English dataset and also on a small hand labelled Bangla corpus. 1.3 Motivation Natural language processing in Bangla language has advanced and evolved in recent years. However, there is room for improvement and further evaluation of natural language processing systems for Bangla is important to strive towards perfection and faster systems. Kågebäck and Salomonsson present a bidirectional long short-term memory network model to disambiguate word sense in their paper [2]. The bidirectional version of the LSTM takes into account two LSTMs in each state, one for words before and one for word after. The model consists of a softmax layer, hidden layer and a bi-directional LSTM. The bidirectional LSTM and hidden layer for all sense and type, share the parameters, while the softmax is parameterized by word type which decides the bias vector and weight matrix for each word type [2]. 15 The proposed BLSTM model by Kågebäck and Salomonsson performed better than previous state- of-the-art score for the Senseval-2 dataset [2]. Work has also been done for word sense disambiguation using neural networks with refined concept co-occurrence information, which is automated and does not require hand coding large data, as presented by Chung, Kang, Moon, and Lee in their paper [8]. executive_digest.findings_and_conclusions: and Future Work 5.1 Conclusion This thesis presented and discussed the effectiveness of word sense disambiguation using supervised learning and a deep neural network classifier on both English and Bangla data. After collecting the SENSEVAL 2 lexical sample data set and applying the individual models, it was evident that the K near neighbors supervised classifier performed with satisfactory results. The accuracy score turned out to be much better than anticipated. On the other hand, the Neural network classifier still has room for improvement. The neural network classifier had significant noise and major variance in accuracy. The neural network implementation requires even further experiments and tweaking in terms of layers, pre-processing and neuron unit count. In both models, the English dataset resulted in more standard and accurate results, since the dataset used, SENSEVAL 2, was a large and standard one. However, the Bangla dataset results are yet to be more accurate, since the data were hand labelled and was relatively small. A larger dataset of Bangla sense tagged data would work even better and would result in a better accuracy score. In general, both the systems were able to perform fairly efficiently and effectively with very fast response time. The systems and implementations presented in this thesis definitely hold practical value in natural language processing and with more experiments, better results can be achieved in the future. 34 5.2 Future Works: There were limitations in analyzing the word sense disambiguation models on Bangla language due to the lack of sense tagged resources. In the future, I would like to further investigate and improve the systems on Bangla using a larger dataset and perhaps newer models. Additionally, I would like to improve the deep learning system and implement it with speech to build a stable and efficient intelligent system that can have a fluid and clear conversation with a human in multiple languages. 35

evaluation.detailed_reasoning: A critical examination of the triad reveals that its exceptionally high pairwise cosine similarities (all between 0.9837 and 0.9855, with a mean of 0.9844 and tightness of 0.9684) are predominantly driven by a corpus-level structural artifact rather than deep foundational domain convergence. All three items in this triad are doctoral dissertations of nearly identical character lengths (~320k to 325k characters: Paper 1 has 325,484 chars; Paper 2 has 321,676 chars; Paper 3 has 320,782 chars) originating from UK/Irish academic repositories. The text embedding model heavily weighted shared macro-structural dissertation features—such as formal front matter, Chapter 1 background expositions, comprehensive literature reviews, academic phrasing ('In this thesis...', 'experimental methods', 'numerical model', 'optimization'), and standard scientific methodology lexicons—collapsing them into an ultra-tight 2-simplex. In reality, their primary thematic domains are disparate: Paper 1 focuses on pharmaceutical formulation science (hydrophilic HPMC K4M swelling matrices, ATR-FTIR compaction spectroscopy, and PLS-2/MCR chemometrics); Paper 2 addresses pulsed laser material processing (DPSS Nd:YVO4 nanosecond laser ablation of Cu/Ti driven by vapor recoil pressure, optical blackening, and localized laser welding of Ag-nanoparticle soda-lime glass to Schott B270); and Paper 3 is centered on experimental and micromagnetic condensed matter physics (manipulation of magnetic anisotropy, dipolar interactions, and OOMMF simulations in nanomodulated Ni45Fe55 permalloy thin films). Nevertheless, beneath this artifactual semantic clustering lies a legitimate, non-trivial methodological complementarity. Paper 2 provides advanced laser-based micro/nanostructuring and hermetic encapsulation techniques; Paper 3 provides the physics and predictive design (OOMMF) of magnetically tunable, anisotropic nanostructures; and Paper 1 provides swelling matrix mechanics and an operando in situ ATR-FTIR chemometric analytical suite. Combining these three distinct toolsets opens legitimate interdisciplinary avenues in remotely triggered smart drug delivery systems, magneto-plasmonic operando dissolution microcells, and micro-electromechanical release devices, justifying an overall score of 5.4 and a verdict of Moderate Methodological Overlap.

research_statements.title: Magneto-Thermally Actuated Hydrophilic Matrices on Laser-Textured Substrates with In Situ ATR-FTIR Release Profiling
research_statements.research_statement: By depositing nanomodulated Ni45Fe55 ferromagnetic thin film arrays (engineered via OOMMF micromagnetic simulations for high hysteretic loss and tailored coercivity) onto nanosecond laser-blackened titanium substrates, alternating magnetic field (AMF) induction will trigger localized thermal deswelling transitions in HPMC K4M matrices, enabling on-demand pulsatile release of basic drugs that can be quantitatively mapped in real time via diamond-ATR-FTIR coupled with multivariate curve resolution (MCR).
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Integrates Paper 3's micromagnetically modeled dipolar coupling and magnetic anisotropy in NiFe thin films for efficient inductive hysteresis heating, Paper 2's nanosecond pulsed laser ablation (which creates high-surface-area micro-cavities for enhanced thermal anchoring and interfacial bonding), and Paper 1's hydrophilic HPMC matrix compaction cell directly onto an ATR crystal for operando chemometric (MCR/PLS-2) tracking of polymer relaxation and drug diffusion.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Establishes a quantitative, mechanistic understanding of how nanoscale magnetic hysteretic heat couples into macromolecular hydrogel relaxation at sub-second temporal resolutions.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Eliminates the empirical guesswork in designing magneto-thermal release systems by directly correlating micromagnetic domain behavior with operando molecular spectroscopic diffusion kinetics.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Implantable and wearable on-demand pulsatile drug delivery patches for circadian-dependent therapeutics, such as analgesics, hormones, and anti-arrhythmic agents.

research_statements.title: Laser-Welded Hermetic Opto-Magnetic Microfluidic Dissolution Cells for Chemometric Tracking of Boundary-Layer Hydrodynamics
research_statements.research_statement: Hermetically sealing nanosecond-laser-welded Ag-nanoparticle soda-lime/Schott B270 glass micro-chambers over nanomodulated NiFe ferromagnetic micropillar arrays will enable contactless, rotating magnetic field-driven micro-vortices that actively regulate boundary-layer diffusion in swelling HPMC/citric acid tertiary matrices, enabling real-time ATR-FTIR chemometric deconvolution of pH-dependent dissolution kinetics under controlled hydrodynamic shear.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Bridges Paper 2's nanosecond laser localized welding of Ag-nanoparticle-doped glass to Schott B270 for robust, transparent micro-dissolution chambers, Paper 3's geometrically modulated NiFe arrays to generate controllable microscale magnetic torque and fluid mixing, and Paper 1's ATR-FTIR compaction and MCR chemometrics to decouple convective shear effects from intrinsic polymer hydration kinetics.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Unravels the coupled mass-transport physics of local convective micro-mixing directly at the polymer-gel dissolution front without disturbing the optical inspection path.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Overcomes the hydrodynamic artifacts and bulk agitation variability inherent to standard USP dissolution apparatuses (baskets/paddles) for micro-scale formulation screening.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: High-throughput microfluidic dissolution testing platforms for preclinical pharmaceutical development, reducing API quantity requirements from grams to micrograms.

research_statements.title: Laser-Patterned Ferromagnetic-Hydrophilic Metamaterials for Field-Directed Transdermal Pulsatile Delivery
research_statements.research_statement: Flexible transdermal drug delivery patches incorporating laser-ablated, microcone-textured titanium foils coated with shape-anisotropic Ni45Fe55 magnetic micro-islands embedded within an HPMC hydrophilic matrix will enable external magnetic gradient-induced mechanical strain pulses to selectively modulate hydration pore networks, achieving tunable zero-order drug release profiles validated by hyphenated ATR-FTIR and NIR spatial chemical imaging.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Leverages Paper 2's 1064 nm nanosecond laser ablation of titanium (generating microcone/micro-cavity topography via vapor recoil pressure that anchors active phases) with Paper 3's dipolar-coupled NiFe nanostructures (which translate external field orientation into localized mechanical shear without vortex breakdown) to mechanically modulate the pore tortuosity of Paper 1's swelling HPMC matrix, with release kinetics resolved using Paper 1's PLS-2/MCR spectral decomposition.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Demonstrates non-thermal, purely magneto-mechanical control of hydrogel pore tortuosity and percolation thresholds via anisotropic dipolar stress fields.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Resolves the burst-release and premature drug leakage common to passively swelling hydrophilic matrices by creating a magnetically gated physical barrier.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Smart transdermal therapeutic systems with physician- or patient-actuated dosing for non-invasive chronic pain management.

research_statements.title: Operando Magneto-Plasmonic Surface-Enhanced ATR-FTIR Sensing of Matrix Hydration Dynamics
research_statements.research_statement: Integrating nanosecond laser-processed Ag-nanocomposite glass substrates with geometrically modulated NiFe ferromagnetic nanoribbons directly onto diamond ATR crystals will enable magneto-plasmonic surface-enhanced infrared absorption (SEIRA), allowing simultaneous real-time chemometric monitoring of polymer relaxation (HPMC chain disentanglement) and magnetic field-steered dissolution of poorly soluble basic drugs across dynamic pH gradients.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Employs Paper 2's laser-processed Ag-nanoparticle glass composite for plasmonic electromagnetic field enhancement, Paper 3's tailored magnetic anisotropy in NiFe thin films to guide and concentrate local mass transport via magneto-hydrodynamic forces, and Paper 1's in situ ATR crystal compaction and PLS/MCR chemometric analytical protocols to track chemical kinetics at sub-nanogram sensitivity.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Achieves single-monolayer sensitivity in tracking the early-stage hydration, glassy-to-rubbery phase transition, and excipient-drug hydrogen bonding in solid dosage forms.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Bypasses the shallow evanescent wave penetration depth (~1-2 µm) limitation of conventional ATR-FTIR by amplifying the interfacial IR signal via plasmonic-magnetic resonance.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Advanced process analytical technology (PAT) and operando analytical instrumentation for continuous pharmaceutical manufacturing and stability testing.

research_statements.title: Remotely Reconfigurable Smart Hydrophilic Implants with Laser-Encapsulated Magnetic Micro-Actuators for Autonomous pH-Responsive Drug Delivery
research_statements.research_statement: An implantable bi-layer controlled-release device comprising a laser-microstructured and welded glass-metal casing (utilizing Ag-nanoparticle soda-lime and Schott B270) encapsulating an OOMMF-designed NiFe bistable magnetic micro-valve will precisely regulate fluid access to a compressed HPMC-citric acid tertiary matrix, where valve switching thresholds and matrix hydration kinetics are calibrated and verified by operando ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and NIR chemical imaging.
research_statements.mechanistic_bridge: Synthesizes Paper 2's laser micro-welding for selective, hermetic biocompatible encapsulation, Paper 3's magnetic anisotropy switching (utilizing remanence and coercivity control in nanomodulated NiFe without continuous power requirements) to act as a micro-gate, and Paper 1's citric acid-acidified HPMC matrix formulation that governs pH-dependent core swelling and drug solubilization, monitored via multivariate spectral analysis.

impact_analysis.scientific_breakthrough: Realizes a zero-standby-power, bistable magneto-fluidic actuator integrated with autonomous chemical feedback derived from internal micro-environmental pH buffers.
impact_analysis.bottleneck_resolved: Solves the chronic reliability and bio-fouling issues of active micro-electromechanical drug delivery systems (BioMEMS) by eliminating onboard batteries and wire interconnects.
impact_analysis.real_world_application: Long-term subcutaneous and gastrointestinal drug delivery implants for automated endocrine therapy (e.g., targeted insulin or glucagon release).

paper_1.title: The use of ATR-FTIR to probe the release mechanism from hydrophilic matrices.

executive_digest.abstract_and_aims: Hydrophilic matrices are widely used in the pharmaceutical industry as control release agents in solid oral dosage formulations. One of the key parameters that controls release in such systems is the distribution of exipients within the formulation, which in turn is governed by the processing and manufacturing procedures. This thesis explores the effect of processing on the distribution of excipients in binary and tertiary formulations obtained using different mixing procedures, (manual shaking, tumble blending and grinding) with a range of particle size distributions. Samples were prepared by compacting processed powder mixtures directly onto a diamond attenuated total reflectance (ATR) crystal using an in-house built compaction cell which proved to be a successful tool for small scale tablet manufacturing. For this study the following exipients were used; the hydrophilic matrix HPMC grade K4M, the drug 6-hydroxy buspirone hydrochloride and citric acid. The homogeneity of the formulations were determined by the reproducibility of the spectra obtained from the tablets after compaction and the concentration of exipients within the samples was successfully predicted using Partial Least Squares (PLS) data analysis. The distribution of the components was confirmed using Near Infrared imaging with principal components analysis (PCA). Standard dissolution tests of the binary and tertiary systems gave an indication about the release behaviour of the formulations in different dissolution media. Total dissolution of the drug was observed in 0.1N HCl for binary mixtures and in both pH 6.8 buffer and 0.1 N HCl for tertiary formulations highlighting the impact of citric acid on the dissolution results and confirming the pH dependence of the system. The release of drug was also studied using the complementary technique of ATR-FTIR by performing hydration experiments on the compacted tablets. executive_digest.introduction_and_motivation: Compressed powder mixtures of one or more hydrophilic polymers with water swelling properties, drug and excipients are called hydrophilic matrices. The ability of hydrophilic polymer matrix systems to provide a desirable drug release profile, cost effectiveness and also broad acceptance of U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) makes them one of the most widely used type of matrices in a controlled release formulation [1, 2]. One of the most commonly used hydrophilic polymers for pharmaceutical formulations is hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC).  This polymer, due to its non toxic nature, non pH dependence and ability to accommodate a large percentage of the drug, fulfills the requirements proposed by the Pifferi and Restani of the modern pharmaceutical excipient [3]. Moreover the ability to hydrate rapidly when in contact with liquid water to form a protective gel around the tablet matrix is an essential HPMC property for drug release [4, 5]. In this introduction the drug release mechanism from hydrophilic matrices along with the properties of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), one of the cellulose derivatives, are discussed, focusing on the use of HPMC as an extended release polymer.  Also the factors influencing the drug release and possible modifications of this process by incorporating pH modifiers into the formulation are included. Finally, the aims of the thesis will be addressed. 2 1.1  Properties of HPMC Cellulose is a linear polymer consisting of anhydroglucose units joined by β 1-4 glycosidic linkages. The substance is insoluble in water due to the presence of inter- and intramolecular hydrogen bonding between hydroxyl groups and the glucose ring oxygen, which influences the high degree of crystallinity. Cellulose contains three reactive hydroxyl groups, two secondary and one primary at the position C-2, C-3 and C-6 atoms on each AGU unit [6, 7]. It is a technology capable of providing an in-sight into the structure and function of modern solid dosage forms. It combines the capability of spectroscopy for molecular analysis with the power of visualization affording precise characterization of the chemical composition, domain structure, and chemical architecture. A NIR Chemical Imaging spectrometer is a solid state system without movable parts so often no calibration of the system is required, the presence of filters allow for specific wavelength image acquisition. There is no need for liquid nitrogen to cool down the system as focal plane array detectors can use electronic cooling to reach the conditions of liquid nitrogen operating temperature. The system allows for imaging of a wide range of samples without previous preparation including samples with uneven or shiny surfaces since the specular glare is removed by polarizers [91, 92]. The technique is useful in the investigation of blend uniformity, raw material and impurity detection and identification [84, 91], pharmaceutical solid dosage form analysis, tablet deconstruction, the content of moisture in excipients or wet granulation mixture as well as in determination of different fabric types and  animal feed studies [84, 91, 114, 118, 119]. 59 2.2.4 Chemometric data analysis The interdisciplinary field which involves using analytical chemistry, multivariate statistics, computer science and mathematical modelling is called chemometrics. paper_2.title: Nanosecond Pulsed Laser Processing of Metals and Welding of Metal-Glass Nanocomposites

executive_digest.abstract_and_aims: 1 Abstract In this thesis, nanosecond pulsed lasers are used as the tools to generate microstructures on metal and glass. The applications of these structures are described too. The production of micro structures is demonstrated using diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) Nd:YVO4 lasers operating at wavelengths of 532nm or 1064 nm. The laser fluence and scanning speed are important parameters to control the results. The first part of thesis is on the laser generation of microstructures on metal surfaces. Copper (Cu) and titanium (Ti) have been studied. According to the reflectivity of metals, Cu is processed by a 532nm laser and Ti is processed by a 1064nm laser. It is shown that the periods of surface microstructures are highly dependent on the hatch distance (overlapping distance between laser scanning). Only if the laser fluence is greater than a threshold, may the microstructures on metals be induced. The thresholds are measured by the diameters of ablated areas at different fluence. Laser generated surface microstructures have been applied to modify the reflectivity of a Cu sample. It was found that laser induced surface microstructures on Copper can decrease the surface reflectivity by almost 97% between 250 nm and 700 nm. To find the mechanism of how to form microstructure on metal surface with laser, laser ablation and heating models have been studied. The 1D ablated numerical model is calculated in Matlab. The pressure of metal vapour is an important parameter, as it pushes the melted metal out of surface to form microstructures after re-solidification. The second part of thesis is on glass welding with microstructures on glass surfaces. The soda-lime glasses containing silver nanoparticles (from the company Abstract 2 Codixx) have been studied and welded with Schott B270 glass. executive_digest.introduction_and_motivation: 1.1 Background Microstructures on materials are not a new concept. Scientists have found many natural microstructures and their novel properties. For example, the leaves of the lotus plant are hydrophobic and developed self cleaning properties because of the double scale roughness with both micron and sub-micron features present [1, 2]. Surfaces that have properties differing from bulk materials can greatly enhance their usefulness in the modern world. Material surfaces structured by laser have many novel characteristics, such as, modified wettability and reflectivity. The microstructures find applications such as electron field emitters [3], and as a model of black body radiation emitter [4]. Understanding and replicating these microstructures on materials were important research topics. Various methods (chemical etching [5], plasma etching [6] and molding [7] of surfaces) can produce micron scale surface topography on metals and other materials [8]. However the laser processing is more simple, convenient and effective. For instance, when the laser is under the control of computer and optical system, the sample surface can be modified with a high degree of accuracy and with little or no excess equipment needed. Microstructures may be directly formed on the surface after the materials are exposed to laser radiation, under inert and reactive ambient gases, with laser wavelengths from UV to IR, and laser pulse lengths from nanoseconds to femtoseconds. They have been observed on many material surfaces (semiconductors [9], metals [10], ceramics [11] and polymer [12]). According to the topography induced by laser, microstructures can be divided into random or highly organised structures. Chapter 1—   Introduction 4 In first case, the microstructures appear at random position after the laser ablation processes, such as spikes on silicon. The structures present many shapes, and are always smaller than the laser spot. They are usually termed microcones or microcolumns because they are approximately conical or cylindrical. The microstructures may be lower than original surface, for instance, in pulsed laser deposition of thin films. The microstructures also may grow out from the target surface, for instance, in surface modification treatments with a range of laser fluencies which have melted a surface layer but the vaporisation rate is low. Sometimes periodic surface structures with a period approximately equal to the laser wavelength are induced by laser. This is easy to explain and understand because of interference [13]. The microstructures induced by multi-pulse laser irradiation have usually a slightly higher period [14]. executive_digest.core_methodology_and_architecture: Chapter 1—   Introduction 6 1.2 Aims and objectives In this project, we research the formation of protruding highly organised microstructures on metal substrates (Cu, Ti) under the cumulative action of nanosecond laser pulses because they may heat, ablate and squeeze the materials during laser irradiation.. The primary aim of the work is to study the relations between microstructures and laser parameters, such as, the number of laser shots, and laser fluence. The highly organized micro-structures were found after irradiation at optimal laser parameters. Examples of highly organized structures on copper are shown in Figure 1-2. One key application of this project is primarily focused on of reflectivity of structured copper surface. Figure 1-2: A 2D optical microscope image of highly organized structures on Cu.  3D optical microscope images and SEM images are in Chapter 3. A second aim of studies presented in the thesis is to find the mechanism of making microstructures by laser, as well as, to optimize the technique of laser-induced modification of the optical properties on metals surface. So a laser ablation model was developed to investigate the initial mechanism of the microstructure growth based on the melt flows caused by the vapour pressure on metal surface. There are the pressure gradients associated with the surface temperature distribution, due to distribution of Chapter 1—   Introduction 7 fluence on laser spot. Therefore, the growth process of new microcones formed on metals was explained as a movement of metals from centre to edge of laser spot. In addition, soda-lime glass containing silver nanoparticles were also processed by nanosecond laser. The mechanism of laser-induced microstructures (bubbles) in this glass has been investigated in laser heating model. The concept of indirectly heating glass though laser interaction with silver nanoparticles has been explored to yield a novel method of jointing or welding separate pieces of glass. The mechanisms responsible for this process have been further investigated. A welded glass sample is shown in Figure 1-3. Figure 1-3: A welded glass sample. It is stuck on a push pin by glue for tensile strength test. 1.3 This work In Chapter 1, a review of previous literatures concerning microstructuring of metals by laser is discussed. paper_3.title: Manipulation of magnetic anisotropy in nanostructures

executive_digest.abstract_and_aims: The magnetic properties of micro/nano-structure have attracted intense research interest in relation to geometrically-induced magnetism to delineate fundamental magnetic phenomena as well as focus the technological aspects in areas such as magnetic sensors, storage devices, integrated inductive components and a number of novel magnetic devices. Depending on the device applications, materials with high, medium or low magnetic anisotropy and their potential manipulation are required. The elements like geometry, crystal structure, magnetic spin configuration at the surfaces and interfaces are the basic ingredients for this manipulation. The most dramatic manifestation in this respect is the chance to manipulate the magnetic anisotropy over the intrinsic preferential direction of the magnetization, commonly observed in all ferromagnetic materials, thus opening up further possibility and functionality of ferromagnetic materials for device applications. In this thesis various types of magnetic anisotropy of different nanostructured materials and their manipulation are investigated. As a first approach detailed experimental and analytical methods for the qualitative and quantitative determination of magnetic anisotropy in nanomodulated Ni45Fe55 thin film are studied. In-plane magnetic ﬁeld rotations in modulated Ni45Fe55 revealed various rotational symmetries of magnetic anisotropy due to dipolar interaction with a crossover from lower to higher fold as a function of modulation geometry. The tendency to form vortex is in fact found to be very small, which highlights that the strong coupling between metastable dipoles is more favorable than vortex formation to minimize energy in this nanomodulated structure. Derived mathematical expressions based on magnetic dipolar interaction and results obtained from Object Oriented Micromagnetic Framework (OOMMF) simulation are found to be in good agreement with our results.
